metrics.name: Headcount
metrics.definition: Total number of employees in the company.

metrics.name: Headcount by department
metrics.definition: Number of employees assigned to each department.
metrics.calculation: SELECT WORKDEPT, COUNT(*) FROM SAMPLE.EMPLOYEE GROUP BY WORKDEPT

metrics.name: Average salary
metrics.definition: Mean annual salary across all employees.

metrics.name: Average salary by department
metrics.definition: Mean annual salary grouped by department.
metrics.calculation: SELECT WORKDEPT, AVG(SALARY) FROM SAMPLE.EMPLOYEE GROUP BY WORKDEPT

metrics.name: Total compensation
metrics.definition: Sum of salary, bonus, and commission per employee.
metrics.calculation: SELECT EMPNO, COALESCE(SALARY,0) + COALESCE(BONUS,0) + COALESCE(COMM,0) AS TOTAL_COMP FROM SAMPLE.EMPLOYEE

metrics.name: Project staffing
metrics.definition: Distinct employees currently working on each project.
metrics.calculation: SELECT PROJNO, COUNT(DISTINCT EMPNO) FROM SAMPLE.EMP_ACT GROUP BY PROJNO

business_rules: SAMPLE is a demo schema shipped with Db2 for i — treat it as read-only. Never run DDL or DML against it.
All identifiers (EMPNO, DEPTNO, PROJNO, MGRNO, WORKDEPT) are fixed-width CHAR columns, not integers. Compare to string literals only.
Every employee has at most one department (WORKDEPT is single-valued); WORKDEPT may be NULL for unassigned employees.
DEPARTMENT.ADMRDEPT and PROJECT.MAJPROJ are self-referential — the schema is hierarchical, not flat.
EMP_ACT is a many-to-many bridge with a composite key — one employee can appear many times for the same (project, activity) pair across different date ranges.
Salaries, bonuses, and commissions are DECIMAL(9,2). For company-wide aggregates, CAST to a wider DECIMAL to avoid overflow on SUM().

common_gotchas.issue: Department / employee numbers treated as integers
common_gotchas.solution: DEPTNO/WORKDEPT are CHAR(3) and EMPNO/MGRNO/RESPEMP are CHAR(6). Compare with string literals: WHERE WORKDEPT = 'A00' and WHERE EMPNO = '000010', never = 10 or = 0.

common_gotchas.issue: Composite key on EMP_ACT produces duplicate rows when projected
common_gotchas.solution: EMP_ACT key is (EMPNO, PROJNO, ACTNO, EMSTDATE). Use SELECT DISTINCT or aggregate when you only want one row per (employee, project).

common_gotchas.issue: Self-referential hierarchies hidden behind simple joins
common_gotchas.solution: DEPARTMENT.ADMRDEPT and PROJECT.MAJPROJ point back at the same table. Use a recursive CTE (WITH RECURSIVE ...) to walk the full tree; root rows in DEPARTMENT have ADMRDEPT equal to their own DEPTNO.

common_gotchas.issue: NULL HIREDATE / BIRTHDATE skews date-math aggregates
common_gotchas.solution: Filter WHERE HIREDATE IS NOT NULL (or BIRTHDATE) before doing AVG / MIN / MAX on derived dates, or use COALESCE with a sentinel before subtracting.
SALARY, BONUS, and COMM are DECIMAL(9,2). For company-wide sums, CAST(SUM(SALARY) AS DECIMAL(15,2)) to keep a safe margin.
